events.title: Medora's Old Fashioned Cowboy Christmas
events.description:
Mark your calendars for December 4-6 and bring the whole family to Medora for a little old-fashioned Christmas magic. Enjoy a weekend filled with family-friendly activities, holiday traditions, small-town charm, and opportunities to make memories that will last a lifetime.

From festive fun to special moments shared with the ones you love, Medora's Old Fashioned Cowboy Christmas is the perfect time to slow down, celebrate the season, and make Medora part of your family's Christmas traditions.

events.title: Medora Mashup Scavenger Hunt
events.description:
Organized by: Kat Nelson, Owner of Alley Kat Adventures — https://www.eventbrite.com/o/27153393487

Explore the hidden gems of the town while getting creative and having fun!

Your creative, nontraditional scavenger hunt begins at a scenic spot that's a local favorite. You'll get your digital quest from your live and interactive remote host. Then you’ll take off on your own to experience a wide variety of carefully curated locations in town. You'll walk or drive to the various checkpoints as you interpret creative tasks, accept wacky challenges, and get outside your comfort zone!

ONE TICKET PER PERSON. Both family and dog friendly, the game alternates between the indoors and outdoors, with plenty of bonus challenges too! You'll text photos and videos to your remote host, who cheers you on and assists, as you play - to document your progress. You can even interact with the locals to interpret the creative challenges. You won’t be able to avoid having fun, uncovering hidden gems and local secrets, making memories, laughing, and learning along the way!

You’ll be part of the rich culture of this dynamic city! Every turn is full of surprises, so questions in advance are welcomed. Check out all 500 of our city hunts! Great for corporate groups, tourists, curious locals, bachelors(ettes), birthdays, families, friend trips, and other special groups! Ask us about our custom-designed experiences and virtual team builders too!

events.title: Midwinter Table: A Badlands Winter Dinner
events.description:
Salted, smoked, cured, cellared, foraged. Midwinter Table is a seated dinner built around the foods that have carried people through Badlands winters.

Executive Chef Candace Stock of Salt + Scoria traces a path from Indigenous foodways through homesteading and ranching to today's regional growers, with chokecherry, prickly pear, blue corn, prairie sage and locally raised beef on the table. Each course features a regional producer, who will be there to explain where the food came from.

When: Friday, December 4. Hosted bar reception at 6 p.m., dinner at 7 p.m. (Mountain) Where: Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, 3410 Chateau Road, Medora Tickets: $150 per person, including the reception and a three-course plated dinner. Add a Black Leg Brewing beer pairing for $25 or a wine pairing for $40.

Ages 21 and older. Seating is limited to 75.

Tickets: https://www.trlibrary.com/midwinter-table

events.title: Girlfriend Getaway 2027
events.description:
About the Girlfriend Getaway

The Girlfriend Getaway was created from a simple belief: women need spaces where they can reconnect with themselves and with each other.

So many of us spend our days caring for everyone else. Managing it all. Showing up for everyone around us. Somewhere along the way, it gets easy to lose touch with ourselves.

This is now our fourth year gathering, and every time, the same thing happens. Women who don’t know a single soul in the room leave feeling like they’ve found their people.

Three days at the Rough Rider Hotel in Medora, ND. Speakers who share real stories, not polished performances. Small group conversations. Time built in just for you: a massage, a facial, reiki, whatever kind of care your body and heart are asking for. And plenty of open space too, to wander Medora, find a coffee shop, read a book, breathe.

You don’t have to come with a plan. You don’t have to come with friends. You just have to come as you are.

If this is your first time, welcome. You’re exactly where you’re meant to be. If you are returning, we can’t wait to see you again.

Ready to grab your spot? Tickets and all the details are linked above. And be sure to tap Going or Interested so you don’t miss updates as we get closer, we’ll be sharing more in the Discussion tab along the way.

events.title: America the Beautiful: Film Screening at the Library
events.description:
America's wild places were not saved by chance. Narrated by Kelsey Grammer, America the Beautiful: Our Natural Wonders travels from sea to shining sea, across mountain ranges, open plains, deserts, rivers and wetlands, and tells the story of the people who protected them, beginning with Theodore Roosevelt.

The film comes to the Library's auditorium in Medora, at the edge of the national park that bears Roosevelt's name, for a two-week run.

Evening screenings: 6:30 p.m. on November 11, 14 and 20 Matinees: Tuesday through Sunday at 2:00 p.m., November 12-25 (no screenings on Mondays) Where: Auditorium, Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, 3410 Chateau Road, Medora Tickets: Adult $7 · Youth $5 · Military $5. Separate ticket required.

Watch the trailer and get tickets: https://www.trlibrary.com/calendar/special-event/america-beautiful-film-screening

events.description:

At the Salt+Scoria counter, build a charcuterie board from local goods to take home or enjoy there. The exhibits stay open all evening, and Santa Claus stops by on December 17 at 6 p.m.

events.title: Books and Banter: The Cloak
events.description:
Join us in the movie room for a monthly book club featuring Victorian-era literature, including titles found in the Chateau library. The book selections are intended to be easy to read and fun to discuss. Coffee and tea will be provided.

November’s book, “The Cloak” by Nickolai Gogol was originally written in Russian, one of the seven languages Medora von Hoffman spoke! The book tells the story of a quiet clerk whose life changes after he buys a new coat.

"The Cloak" is available to read for free via Project Gutenberg. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/13437

events.title: Books and Banter: A Christmas Carol
events.description:
Join us in the movie room for a monthly book club featuring Victorian-era literature, including titles found in the Chateau library. The book selections are intended to be easy to read and fun to discuss. Coffee and tea will be provided.

December’s book, “A Christmas Carol” by Charles Dickens, tells the story of Ebenezer Scrooge, a bitter man who changes his ways after visits from three ghosts. Through their lessons, he learns kindness, generosity, and the true meaning of Christmas. This Victorian novella helped establish Christmas traditions in Great Britain and beyond.

"A Christmas Carol" is available to read for free via Project Gutenberg. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/20673
